inventory.test: (no executable covering test) PG17 MAINTAIN branch, supabase/migrations/122_client_role_grant_sweep.sql:108-114
inventory.reason: The local and CI container is PostgreSQL 16 (server_version_num 160014; .github/workflows/ci.yml:252 image postgres:16), so the IF branch never runs and no test can kill a mutant of it. Not mutated: a survivor would be unexecuted by construction. Out-of-suite check on a throwaway postgres:17-alpine container (170010, 22 synthetic RLS tables, default ALL grants): the verbatim file applied twice without error, the four-right has_table_privilege count was 0, reviews kept 8 client DML rights, service_role kept MAINTAIN on all 22, and a rolled-back new-table probe showed client DML only. That is evidence the SQL is correct, not a test oracle.

inventory.test: (no executable covering test) SET LOCAL lock_timeout backstop, supabase/migrations/122_client_role_grant_sweep.sql:70
inventory.reason: Only a contention path can tell this line apart, and no test sets up contention. Not proven equivalent: lock_timeout also bounds waits on pg_class tuple locks from a concurrent GRANT. Direct probe on throwaway PG17 confirms the header claim that REVOKE takes no relation lock (it finished under a held ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and under a held ROW EXCLUSIVE with lock_timeout 1s).

First baseline (BA) was red for infra: tsx IPC socket path under the long scratch TMPDIR exceeded the unix socket limit (EINVAL listen); rerun with a short tmp home: BA2 passed. MA1 (delete the entry) -> failed: runtime-ddl on the 122 suite (first at line 241).

Unchanged importer of the changed module. Every case feeds synthetic file content and never reads the real MIGRATION_SHAPE_FILES membership of the 122 path, so it cannot cover a data-only entry. INV-10 measures that hunk instead.

findings.title: Two production hunks in migration 122 have no executable covering test: the PG17-only MAINTAIN branch and the lock_timeout backstop. The only proof is the mandatory post-apply PG17 query on each project.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Uncovered-change rule: no test in the inventory executes lines 108-114 on PG16, and none creates lock contention for line 70. The intake records the PG16 limit (edge_cases, observability) and makes the PG17 four-right query mandatory, but that is a manual step, not a test oracle. Throwaway PG17 checks by the red team found no defect (INV-8, INV-9). High-risk migration: the user must adjudicate.

findings.title: The suite restore reverts only grants and the default ACL. A migration change that alters RLS flags or policies leaves the shared local test DB dirty after the run.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Seen under mutant M4b: agent_runs stayed FORCE RLS after the suite finished and had to be reset by hand. In-run detection still works (INV-4 killed). This matters only for a defective edit to the migration, and the shipped file changes no RLS state.
